findings.text: Provides early 64-bit startup routine that accepts a physical to virtual offset plus boot parameters and returns a startup postprocessing result. It establishes identity and kernel mappings before handing off to later SME handling.

Provides SNP CPUID resolution service that consults a validated table and an optional hypervisor callback to fill a leaf structure. It reports unsupported when no table entries exist and otherwise returns postprocessing status.
Provides a virtualization exception handler for environments without a shared communication page. It only services CPUID exits and terminates the guest for any other exit or validation failure.

Provides early helper to request private page state for a virtual and physical range of given page count. It has no effect when SNP enablement is absent and otherwise forwards to a page state changer with a private descriptor.

Provides early SNP initialization predicate that locates confidential blob information, validates secrets placement, prepares CPUID data and SVSM communication, caches the blob location, and reports success.

Serves as 64-bit boot entry that validates load address bounds and alignment, computes a relocated base including encryption mask, repairs static page tables, creates temporary identity coverage, sanitizes kernel image range, then invokes SME postprocessing.

Serves as exception entry receiving register state and an exit code. It extracts function and subfunction from general registers, validates opcode bytes at the instruction pointer, resolves CPUID, enforces SEV presence checks, advances past the instruction or terminates.
Serves as boot time SNP probe invoked with boot parameters. It returns false when parameters or blob or secrets are missing or malformed, otherwise completes table and SVSM setup and returns true.

Carries page population context with a bump allocator cursor for fresh tables, a root table pointer, separate flag selections for middle and leaf levels, a physical placement cursor, plus virtual start and end bounds for the range being mapped.

Pairs generic setup chaining header with a 32-bit confidential blob address field, allowing firmware or loader to convey blob location through setup data when boot parameters do not carry it directly.

Upper walk creates missing intermediate tables on demand, clears each new table fully, advances the shared allocator cursor by whole table size, installs entries with table-only flags combined with physical placement, preserves existing entries, and aborts with null when encountering a large leaf at upper level.

Lower walk reuses the upper walk result, allocates a leaf table only when the middle entry is empty, respects large middle leaves by returning without change, and installs a leaf mapping only when the leaf slot is empty, using supplied physical cursor and leaf flags.
Range mapper for small pages advances virtual and physical cursors in lockstep by single page granularity, invoking single page population for each step until the virtual end bound is reached.

Table size estimator conservatively counts directory, middle and lower tables proportional to range length with an extra entry for misalignment, adds at most two leaf pages for unaligned edges, then adds second order tables needed to map the estimator output itself, omitting top directory on four level builds.

Startup validates that the running physical address fits within allowed physical bits and that the relocated base respects large page alignment, halting without progress if either check fails, and folds the memory encryption mask into fixup deltas and table flags.

Temporary identity coverage uses unencrypted table flags plus encryption mask, avoids the global attribute on transitional entries, writes paired entries to tolerate wraparound, selects a four or five level shape based on address width support, and maps the whole kernel image extent with large executable entries.

Kernel image sanitization clears presence before the image start, adjusts present entries inside the image by the relocated delta, clears presence after the image end, and adjusts static kernel and fixmap tables by the same delta to reflect actual load placement.

Hypervisor CPUID fetch over MSR rejects indexed functions with nonzero subfunction, otherwise queries four registers individually through a request exit and response code check, propagating first failure and succeeding only when all four succeed.

Extended save size computation starts from legacy base size, scans validated entries for extended state leaves, considers only enabled and previously unseen features, accumulates either by summation for compacted form or by maximum extent otherwise, and returns zero when observed features do not match requested mask.

Validated lookup scans the SNP table for matching function and, for indexed functions, matching subfunction, restricts extended state base leaves to legacy control values with no supervisor mask, copies all four register outputs on match and reports success, otherwise reports absence.

Top level SNP CPUID returns unsupported when the table is empty, otherwise attempts validated lookup, and on miss zero fills outputs while still running postprocessing for in-range standard, hypervisor and extended functions but skipping postprocessing for out-of-range leaves.

Postprocessing merges hypervisor and validated values per leaf: preserves low identification bits while taking initial APIC and enablement bits from hypervisor for base leaf, refreshes protection keys enablement from control register, takes extended APIC identifiers from hypervisor for topology leaves, and recomputes extended save size from live control and supervisor masks with compaction and feature checks.

After successful CPUID resolution the handler enforces that the highest basic extended leaf reaches the security leaf and that the security leaf reports the memory encryption capability bit, terminating the guest if either assurance fails, otherwise writing back all four registers.

Blob locator prefers direct address from boot parameters when present, otherwise searches setup data chain, returns null when no candidate exists, validates a magic header value on any candidate and terminates the guest on mismatch.

Secure module setup records the calling area when not at highest privilege, obtains its address with position independent reference while identity mapped, issues a remap request through MSR protocol, terminates on failure and caches physical placement. Initialization requires page sized secrets, then prepares CPUID data, runs module setup, and caches blob address for later use.

Private memory request builds a descriptor selecting private state with boot time calling area references, checks SNP enablement through a direct status flag to avoid jump tables or per CPU data while identity mapped, and returns immediately when SNP is inactive.
Two thin wrappers select decrypted versus decrypted write protected flag pairs and delegate to a common range mapper, centralizing mode specific flag choice outside the page walk.
Secure CPUID hypervisor callback treats any MSR fetch failure as fatal and terminates with a Linux specific CPUID reason instead of returning partial register contents.

SME mapping progresses from top directory through intermediate levels to middle and leaf tables, with states for reuse of present entries, allocate and clear plus install for empty entries, and early exit for large leaves or null upper result, ending in conditional leaf install.

Resolution moves from table presence check to validated lookup, then either postprocess on hit or zero fill plus range test on miss, followed by selective postprocess, while hypervisor fetch failures in secure contexts transition to termination rather than returning data.

Exception flow validates exit reason then instruction encoding, attempts SNP table resolution with hypervisor callback, falls back to direct hypervisor query only on unsupported status, enforces security leaf assurances, then either advances past the instruction on success or terminates on any prior failure.

Initialization advances from parameter presence to blob discovery to secrets validation to CPUID table setup to module setup to blob caching, with early false return on missing inputs and termination on header or communication failures.

Boot startup advances through width detection, address validation, delta computation, static table repair, temporary identity construction with width dependent shape, kernel range sanitization, and SME postprocessing return, with halting states on validation failure.
Out of range physical placement or misaligned relocated base causes an intentional infinite halt, preventing continued boot with unmappable or incorrectly aligned image placement.

Multiple integrity failures terminate the guest instead of continuing with untrusted data: hypervisor CPUID protocol mismatch, indexed subfunction over MSR, extended save size failure, blob header mismatch, module remap failure, unsupported exit or opcode, and missing security leaf or capability bit.

Entries outside the verified kernel image extent are explicitly marked not present so that speculative access cannot reach reserved firmware areas that on some platforms trigger fatal physical errors, with later cleanup expected to repair any provisional invalid entries.

Encountering a large leaf at upper or middle level suppresses further table creation and leaf installation for that address, so a preexisting large mapping silently shadows the requested small mapping without error indication.

Mismatch between requested extended features and validated table coverage yields a zero size that callers treat as invalid, preventing use of an undersized save area that would corrupt extended processor state.

Table levels share a common unencrypted table flag baseline, while large executable mappings derive from a kernel large executable baseline without the global attribute, and small executable mappings derive from a kernel executable baseline likewise without global.

Decrypted modes reuse the executable baselines unchanged, encrypted modes add the memory encryption attribute, and write protected decrypted modes replace caching attributes with write through plus uncached style combinations to force visibility during transitions.
Early SME work area reserves space equal to two large page units in the init scratch section, providing transient storage for page construction before general allocation is available.

Postprocessing and validation recognize designated processor identification functions including base feature, extended feature, topology enumeration, extended state enumeration, plus hypervisor and extended ranges delimited by stored maxima, with special handling for security and topology extended leaves.

Early code uses position independent addressing for static tables, read-only-after-init storage for the SNP table copy and range maxima, an identity address helper, a selector for five level early tables, a feature test delegation, a boolean warning coercion, and a log prefix marking security messages.
